guideposts.label: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 2 of La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: After the opening ITT and Manosque's sprint, the peloton of La Vuelta 26 face a first muntain challenge with a summit finish at Font-Romeu. The line is set atop a cat. 2 ascent, coming in quick succession after the first cat. 1 climb of this edition. But the road is flat to begin with. Will it favour long range attackers or GC contenders? The neutral start is set at 13:10, the start proper at 13:2

guideposts.label: Gruissan, back on a Grand Tour map
guideposts.detail: Gruissan is a La Vuelta stage town for the second time. On the first occasion, in 2017, it was the finish for stage 2, after the Gran Salida in Nîmes. In the finale, the bunch exploded, Yves Lampaert attacked with 1 km to go, and the Belgian eventually took the stage and La Roja. Gruissan also appeared on the map of the Tour de France, in 2024. guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: With Matthew Brennan (1st), Ben Tulett (11th) and Wout van Aert (22nd) in the first positions, Visma-Lease a Bike had the best collective performance yesterday. They remain second in the team standings, 3 seconds behind UAE Emirates XRG. Netcompany Ineos are now third (+23’’).

guideposts.label: First attack
guideposts.detail: Six riders try to get away from the peloton.

guideposts.label: 30 seconds
guideposts.detail: Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) is among the riders on the move.

guideposts.label: Hayter is back on the move
guideposts.detail: The six early attackers: Olivier Le Gac (Groupama-FDJ United), Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility), Asbjorn Hellemose (Jayco AlUla), Timo Roosen (Pinic PostNL), and Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma). At km 5, Milan Vader (Bahrain Victorious) is chasing with a gap of 42''. The peloton trail by 51''.

guideposts.label: The break gets away
guideposts.detail: At km 8, Vader is 45'' behind the six leaders, and the peloton are 45'' further behind.

guideposts.label: Vader is caught by the bunch
guideposts.detail: They are now 2'05'' behind the six leaders.

guideposts.label: Gap under control?
guideposts.detail: Olivier Le Gac (Groupama-FDJ United), Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility), Asbjorn Hellemose (Jayco AlUla), Timo Roosen (Pinic PostNL) and Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) head to km 25 with a lead of 2'15''.

guideposts.label: An update from Uijtdebroeks
guideposts.detail: At the start, Cian Uijtdebroeks (Movistar) spoke about his sensations after he crashed yesterday: “That was a tough night, let’s say, but I’m here! The body feels quite OK, just the feet is a little bit of a problem. There’s maybe like a small fissure, we cannot see a lot because there’s fluid around, but let’s see how it is on the bike and what we can do. You know, for sure I wanted to finish yes

guideposts.label: The gap increases to 2'40''
guideposts.detail: The breakaway riders are at km 37.

guideposts.label: The gap decreases
guideposts.detail: After reaching a maximum of 2'40'', the gap is back down to 2 minutes.

guideposts.label: 45.7 km covered in the first hour
guideposts.detail: The attackers are pushing hard to get away. But the peloton are not giving much leeway.

guideposts.label: Cort to chase a final La Vuelta stage win?
guideposts.detail: Among the six attackers, Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) is the most experienced and the most decorated. The Danish all rounder is participating in his 5th La Vuelta, his 15th and final Grand Tour as he has announced he will retired at the end of the season, at 33 years old. guideposts.label: 2'35'' at km 64
guideposts.detail: Tadej Pogacar's teammates still control the gap.

guideposts.label: UAE Team Emirates XRG leading the peloton
Hard pace in the bunch
guideposts.detail: The attackers are 95 kilometres from the finish and the gap is down to 1'40''. The bunch is very stretched.

guideposts.label: The peloton is chasing the breakaway
Stragglers get back to the bunch, including Gall
guideposts.detail: The pace appears to drop in the first peloton. Domen Novak (UAE Emirates XRG) sits up to wait for Joao Almeida, who was at his team car when the bunch exploded.

guideposts.label: The breakaway are not giving up easily
Memories from Font-Romeu
guideposts.detail: Font-Romeu makes its debut as a Grand Tour stage finish. La Vuelta passed here in 2001, on stage 11, a day marked by two emblematic figures of the race. In the 8th of his 17 consecutive participations, Iñigo Cuesta went first at the summit early in the stage. guideposts.label: Alex Kirsch abandons
guideposts.detail: He is the second rider out of La Vuelta 26 after Sergio Chumil's crash yesterday.

guideposts.label: Into the final 50 kilometres
guideposts.detail: Olivier Le Gac (Groupama-FDJ United), Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility), Asbjorn Hellemose (Jayco AlUla), Timo Roosen (Pinic PostNL) and Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) are headed for the intermediate sprint with a lead back up to 2 minutes.

guideposts.label: The average speed after three hours: 43.3 km/h
guideposts.detail: The peloton just passed the intermediate sprint with a gap of 1'40''. Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) was first across the line.

guideposts.label: Hellemose accelerates
guideposts.detail: As the gap drops down to 30 seconds, Asbjorn Hellemose (Jayco AlUla) accelerates with 28 km to go. Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) and Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) follow him.

guideposts.label: Wenzel ups the ante with 25 km to go
guideposts.detail: Only Cort follows the young climber. They are 8.5 km away from the summit. Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates-XRG) pulls the bunch with a gap of 30 seconds.

guideposts.label: Cort is caught by the bunch
guideposts.detail: Wenzel is the last rider from the breakaway still ahead of the bunch. His lead is up to 48'' with 6.5 km to the summit.

guideposts.label: Fortunato in pursuit
guideposts.detail: Lorenzo Fortunato (XDS Astana) has attacked from the bunch to try and chase Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) before the summit.

guideposts.label: Fortunato is with Wenzel
guideposts.detail: They are inside the last kilometre of ascent to Col de Mont-Louis. The peloton trail by 25''.
